income.label: Income
income.title: Safe income town
income.intro: Interior settlement with no unique recruiting or strategic job.

steps.title: Weaving House
steps.note: Get a straightforward income source running before paying for optional infrastructure.

steps.title: Fields while developing
steps.note: Build growth while developing the province. The farm chain also supports local army replenishment.

steps.title: Upgrade main settlement for useful slots
steps.note: Do not upgrade only to stare at another empty slot you cannot afford to fill.

steps.title: Industry → resource / control utility
steps.note: Resource, basic recruitment or public order depending on the province—not a complete second military complex.

steps.title: Retain recovery; replace surplus growth
steps.note: Keep a farm in a recovery province where its replenishment still matters.

details: A three-slot working plan

Industry + Fields + resource/utility is the default, counting buildable slots rather than the settlement’s main building. A port or landmark changes the available space; do not force an impossible layout.
No Bretonnian farm/industry balancing
This guide does not apply Bretonnia’s peasant economy to the Empire. Choose buildings for their actual income, growth and replenishment effects.

resource.label: Resource
resource.title: Resource or valuable landmark settlement
resource.intro: The local resource can be the main reason this place deserves a permanent slot in your realm.

steps.title: Repair resource / valuable landmark
steps.note: Compare its income and useful modifiers with a generic industry investment.

steps.title: Fields while its province develops
steps.note: Growth helps unlock the next valuable tier; do not add redundant growth just to follow a pattern.

steps.title: Industry in the spare economic slot
steps.note: Use remaining space to produce income rather than duplicate advanced recruitment.

steps.title: Upgrade the valuable chain
steps.note: A resource on an undefended border is not guaranteed income.

steps.title: Defence or utility if the location needs it
steps.note: Protect a mine town if losing it would collapse the budget.

details: Pastures are a useful exception

The Empire’s Grazing Pastures combine income with growth and replenishment. Treat their own benefits as part of your growth/recovery plan; do not count the town as having no growth simply because you did not build generic Fields.
Keep or transfer
A useful resource still has to pass your border test. A disconnected outpost that needs its own army can be worse than a smaller safe realm.

recovery.label: Recovery
recovery.title: Provincial recovery and support base
recovery.intro: Especially useful in newly secured Sylvania or at the near end of an expedition.

steps.title: Repair the settlement and working income
steps.note: Avoid developing a city you intend to give away immediately.

steps.title: Fields for recovery
steps.note: Adds growth and local army replenishment; use this as a place to recover after costly autoresolves.

steps.title: Shrine → Temple of Sigmar if needed
steps.note: Temple of Sigmar is a tier-3 destination providing Warrior Priest recruitment and capacity.

steps.title: Inn / Tavern when locally useful
steps.note: Tavern upkeep applies to armies in its region, not automatically to every army in the province or faction.

steps.title: One support chain; then income
steps.note: A local Captain, Priest or Wizard source can be worthwhile; four redundant military chains usually are not.

details: Recovery and attrition are different
Reducing incoming attrition is not the same as increasing replenishment. Elspeth’s personal protections also do not automatically belong to every new army.
Replenish before the next commitment
A narrow victory that cripples the force may require a return here. That turn of recovery is part of campaign tempo, not a failed build.
A Garden is an additional system
Black Tower regional replenishment support is especially useful outside your own lands. Militia support and other bonuses have explicit scopes; do not silently apply local effects factionwide.

frontier.label: Frontier
frontier.title: A settlement that guards a real approach
frontier.intro: Choose a few defensive anchors rather than fortifying every quiet interior town.

steps.title: Repair; inspect the enemy’s real approach
steps.note: Estimate which enemy army can reach it next turn before starting luxury construction.

steps.title: Useful garrison / defence chain
steps.note: Read the actual garrison it provides. Do not assume every defensive building creates walls in a minor settlement.

steps.title: Fields or other local recovery
steps.note: Useful when a responding army must replenish here between attacks.

steps.title: Industry after credible defence
steps.note: A border settlement must eventually support its own cost.

steps.title: Keep a responding field force in reach
steps.note: Buildings buy time; they do not defeat every full stack without help.

details: Fort Soll is a special case

Treat a fort’s unique main building and garrison as its own defensive system, not as a normal town with this exact three-building recipe. Defend the southern approach without automatically marching into a new southern conquest.
Keep strategic depth

Defensible terrain is useful, but mobile enemies, alternative routes and special movement can still bypass a single position. Retain a small response force rather than declaring the border invulnerable.

temporary.label: Temporary
temporary.title: Expedition capture / future handover
temporary.intro: Winning a battle does not automatically make the captured settlement part of your permanent realm.

steps.title: Read the live VCO requirement
steps.note: Confirm whether this is an objective settlement, a search candidate or merely a staging point.

steps.title: Repair only for the next operation
steps.note: Avoid expensive multi-tier development before a planned transfer.

steps.title: Stage, replenish and scout
steps.note: A temporary capture can be useful without becoming a distant recruitment centre.

steps.title: Keep or transfer to a trusted partner
steps.note: Use the settlement-trading options actually available in your game. This guide does not assume Trade Any Settlement is installed.

steps.title: Recheck credit after any handover
steps.note: Especially important when a route accepts diplomatic control. Do not equate an ordinary trade agreement with objective ownership.

details: An explicit budget boundary
No automatic landmark upgrades, no second military complex, and no confederation solely because the button becomes available. Spend to achieve the operation’s purpose.
Route 3 warning
The author lists possible search locations but not a universal numerical quota. Do not turn a candidate list into an invented requirement to own every candidate simultaneously.

nuln.label: Nuln
nuln.title: Nuln · foundry and field-test centre
nuln.intro: Concentrate expensive advanced production here. Distribute basic recruiting and growth into the rest of the province.

steps.title: Protect Nuln; growth + income nearby
steps.note: Keep useful starting military buildings until another settlement can do their job. Repair or build industry and Fields nearby. A strict demolition plan is worse than using your actual starting assets.

steps.title: T2: Firearms Academy + Gunsmith
steps.note: These are two separate chains. Field Testing needs the named Firearms Academy and three Handgunners; do not immediately replace every Handgunner with an Ironside.

steps.title: T3: Gunnery School + Foundry
steps.note: The shooting chain also supplies Witch Hunter capacity. The Forges chain supplies Engineer recruitment/capacity and meets the named Foundry test.
steps.short: Ironsides, Long Rifles and Great Cannons.

steps.title: Nuln Cannon Foundry landmark
steps.note: Build the tier-three landmark when the treasury can support it without cancelling your working army or response force. It has a different slot from ordinary Forges and the Marksman chain.

steps.title: T4: Engineer’s Workshop
steps.note: The tier-four Forges upgrade unlocks the main late-game artillery/machine transition. Take units that solve the route’s job; a Land Ship is not an obligatory purchase.
steps.short: Helstorms, Volley Guns and Land Ships.

steps.title: T5: landmark; advanced machines as needed
steps.note: Nuln Gunnery School is the tier-five LANDMARK, needed by the final published Field Testing stage. Ordinary tier-three Gunnery School does not satisfy it. Advanced Steam Tank production follows the higher Forges tier.
steps.short: Finish Field Testing only when worthwhile.

details: Three different “schools”

The ordinary Gunnery School is a tier-three recruiting building. Nuln Gunnery School is a tier-five landmark. Imperial Gunnery School is the faction interface with Field Testing and upgrade tiers. They are not interchangeable.
What leaves the capital

A tier-three minor can host a Livery for Black Rose knights and Theodore’s initial task, or a Temple of Sigmar for Priests. A Rally Field can handle the basic infantry. Plan one role per town around available slots; do not assume unlimited room.
Growth timing

Accelerate Nuln to tier three for the working army and tier four for the artillery/machine transition. Tier five is a separate late investment, not the point at which the campaign is finally allowed to begin.

military.label: Support town
military.title: Military support town · the missing profession
military.intro: Use a tier-three settlement in the recruiting province to provide what Nuln’s limited slots cannot.

steps.title: Choose ONE support job
steps.note: Do not reproduce all four jobs in every minor. First inspect what the province already offers.

steps.title: Rally Field for infantry support
steps.note: Upgrade the Barracks chain only when the extra troop or hero capacity is useful. A tier-two destination can already support a practical gunline.

steps.title: OR Livery for the Black Rose escort
steps.note: The tier-three Livery is a sensible cavalry investment when two Black Rose units will accompany your main army. It is an alternative role, not the next slot in every town.

steps.title: OR Temple of Sigmar / Wizard’s Conclave
steps.note: The Temple is a tier-three Priest recruitment/capacity destination; Wizard’s Conclave is the initial wizard chain. Check hero capacity separately from the recruit button.
steps.short: Supply the planned hero, not a collection.

steps.title: Industry in the next spare slot
steps.note: Retain a resource or useful port rather than demolishing it to follow a generic recipe.
steps.short: Let the support town help pay for itself.

steps.title: Fields or defence in the last slot
steps.note: Once growth is no longer useful, switch only when its recovery benefits are also unnecessary.
steps.short: Growth until developed; defence if exposed.

details: These are alternatives
Steps two to four name mutually competing town roles, not a requirement to put all three chains into one minor. Choose the role once, then develop that building to its stated useful tier.
Hero acquisition is staged

One Engineer and a Priest in the first developed army are useful. Additional capacity matters when you can actually recruit and embed the next hero. Theodore’s arrival replaces a Captain; it does not expand the twenty-slot limit.

charter.label: Charter hub
charter.title: Southern charter capital · a second production centre
charter.intro: A permanent regional hub is justified when the southern theatre is too far from Nuln for convenient replacements.

steps.title: Keep the whole strategic province
steps.note: Prefer a connected capital with a port/resource and defensible approach. Miragliano is a natural candidate when held safely, not an instruction to attack a friendly owner.
steps.short: Confirm ownership and the route checklist.

steps.title: Repair income / port → Fields
steps.note: Do not spend all conquest proceeds on new production before control, corruption and the garrison are stable.

steps.title: Gunnery School to T3
steps.note: Add the ordinary Marksman chain. This is the minimum regional recruiting upgrade; not another rush to Nuln’s unique landmark.

steps.title: Forges to T3; T4 only for demand
steps.note: Build advanced Forges when several nearby armies or persistent casualties justify the travel saved. A one-off expedition does not need a second complete industrial capital.

steps.title: A legal Garden: Militia by default
steps.note: Select it only if the settlement is actually eligible in the Gardens panel. Non-Empire allied ports are not automatically eligible.

steps.title: Defence + route-specific utility
steps.note: Build garrison, temple or control support for the actual threat. Keep peripheral treaty partners rather than annexing them for neat map colours.
steps.short: Protect access to the production centre.

details: Two army roles, not two luxury stacks
Elspeth leads the hard push; the regional Master Engineer takes over cleared fronts and protects production. Upgrade their army cores before adding a third expedition you cannot support.
Why this is route-specific
Route II asks for maintained provincial control. Investing in one southern centre is therefore much more attractive than building the same infrastructure at every Route III search stop.

survey.label: Foothold
survey.title: Survey foothold · an expedition service station
survey.intro: Keep the northern Badlands expedition alive without turning every candidate into a five-tier project.

steps.title: Select access, safety and a useful location
steps.note: Pick a place that supports the next candidate cluster and has a believable route back. A ruin is not good merely because it appears on the VCO list.

steps.title: Repair settlement → Fields
steps.note: Check actual replenishment and attrition in the province. Do not assume an alliance alone grants recovery everywhere.

steps.title: Income or resource that pays back
steps.note: Low-climate profitability, control and future ownership affect whether this investment is worthwhile.
steps.short: Fund the operation while it is present.

steps.title: Basic line and gun replacements
steps.note: Advanced Forges are optional only after the expedition becomes a persistent theatre. Global recruitment is an expensive but valid bridge.

steps.title: A Garden only in an eligible Empire town
steps.note: Dwarf ownership can help VCO diplomatic search without permitting a Garden. Keep the two systems separate.
steps.short: Militia for recovery; College for a safe node.

steps.title: Reassess when the fortress is found
steps.note: Confirm any remaining VCO instructions before transferring. Do not continue buying infrastructure just because construction space exists.
steps.short: Keep, hand over, or consolidate deliberately.

details: Do not make the reward a prerequisite
The Route III reward includes a follower and research/loot benefits, not a verified flying-fortress unit. The expedition must work before any reward appears.
Conquest is one way to investigate
An appropriate alliance may satisfy the live mission. When it does, do not declare war on the same Dwarf partner to duplicate already-credited work.
